$comment: Business scenarios SC-01..SC-12 from BRD section 6, plus SC-99 (implementation decision AD-001). Keywords are EVIDENCE SIGNALS used for corroboration and few-shot context - they are NOT the classification mechanism (BRD section 28). Seed for Dataverse spa_businessscenario.

scenarios.scenarioName: Learner cannot advance in FIT/FLO journey
scenarios.description: A learner is unable to progress through their FIT or FLO journey: they cannot move to the next island, cannot submit a questionnaire or survey, a control is greyed out, or their data was not saved.
positiveExamples: I finished island 3 but the Next button is greyed out and I cannot move on.
I keep having trouble submitting the week 2 questionnaire - it says data not saved.
I am stuck on the survey and cannot proceed to the next section of my FLO journey.
negativeExamples: I cannot log in to FIT at all - the authenticator keeps failing.
Thank you, I am able to work through the modules now.
Please remove this learner from PEP Passport, they have left the business.

escalationRule.$comment: GAP-010 - the BRD does not define how 'issue persists' is detected or how long to wait. Disabled until Business answers Q-09.

scenarios.scenarioName: FIT/FLO login, access, authenticator or cache issue
scenarios.description: A user cannot sign in to or access FIT or FLO. Includes authenticator failures, browser cache problems, missing access permissions, and users who are not registered or enrolled.
positiveExamples: I am unable to access FIT - the authenticator app never sends me a code.
It says I am not registered when I try to sign in to FLO.
I cleared my cache but I still cannot access the platform.
negativeExamples: I can log in fine but the Next button on island 4 is greyed out.
My manager needs access to see my check-ins.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Monday.

escalationRule.$comment: GAP-010 - same as SC-01. BRD states the troubleshooting response is sent before escalation where applicable.

scenarios.description: A request concerning a learner's manager: assigning a new manager, correcting a manager ID or manager email, a manager needing access to check-ins, or a direct supervisor change. A request to CHANGE the manager follows the formal PEP Passport change-request process; a manager who cannot technically access what they should already see is a technical issue for the programme owner.
positiveExamples: My manager has changed - please update my direct supervisor to Jane Smith.
The manager ID on my profile is wrong, it should be 1234567.
My manager cannot see my check-ins even though she is listed as my supervisor.
negativeExamples: I cannot log in to FLO at all.
Please remove me from PEP Passport, I have left the company.
My peer trainer does not appear in the dropdown.

scenarios.scenarioName: Pep Passport change request form notification / acknowledgement
scenarios.description: A system-generated notification that a PEP Passport Change Request Form response was received, or an acknowledgement that a submitted request was completed. Machine generated, no human is waiting on a reply.
keywords: New response for Pep Passport Change Request Form
positiveExamples: New response for Pep Passport Change Request Form
We have received and completed your request. Request ID: CR-102934.
Thank you, you have submitted your request. Request ID 88213.
negativeExamples: Please submit a change request to have my manager updated.
I completed island 2 but cannot advance.
Automatic reply: out of office.

scenarios.scenarioName: Peer trainer access / trainer not showing in dropdown
scenarios.description: A peer trainer cannot be selected or does not appear in the trainer dropdown, or a trainer needs to be assigned or changed for skills checks. A trainer CHANGE follows the change-request process; an existing trainer with a technical access problem goes to the programme owner.
positiveExamples: My peer trainer does not show her name in the dropdown when I complete a skills check.
Please assign a new peer trainer for this learner.
The trainer has access but cannot sign off the skills check.
negativeExamples: My manager needs to be changed.
I cannot access FIT at all.
Thanks, the trainer shows up now.

scenarios.description: A request to remove a learner from PEP Passport or FLO, because the employee has left the organisation, or because they were duplicated across both onboarding paths.
positiveExamples: Please remove John Doe from PEP Passport, he is no longer with the organization.
This learner is duplicated across both onboarding paths - please remove the FLO record.
Employee no longer employed, remove from FLO.
negativeExamples: Please update this learner's email address.
The learner cannot advance past island 2.
Please change this learner's manager.

scenarios.description: Anything relating to the Merch Effectiveness Coach (MEC) pathway, the Schoox platform, CGR, MEC workweeks, decks, resources, capstone or MEC responsibilities.
positiveExamples: Where can I find the MEC workweek 3 deck on Schoox?
Question about the Merch Effectiveness Coach capstone requirements.
CGR pathway resources are not loading in Schoox.
negativeExamples: I cannot advance in my FLO journey.
Please update my manager.
Automatic reply: out of office.

escalationRule.$comment: BRD: do NOT route to FIT/FLO owners unless the email contains a separate FIT/FLO issue. Enforced by the multi-intent resolver rule MI-SCHOOX-PLUS.

scenarios.description: A machine-generated automatic reply or out-of-office notice. Carries no actionable content.
positiveExamples: Automatic reply: I am out of the office with limited access to email.
Out of Office: for urgent issues please contact my colleague.
I am currently out of the office and will have limited access to email.
negativeExamples: I am out of ideas, I still cannot log in.
My manager is out of office so please update my supervisor.
Thank you for the quick response.

scenarios.description: A request about dashboard access, location visibility, a full location view, or reporting. A request to GRANT access or widen visibility follows the change-request process; a dashboard that is broken or showing wrong data is a technical issue for the programme owner.
positiveExamples: Please give me dashboard access for my full location view.
The dashboard is not showing any of my direct reports even though I have access.
I need reporting visibility for the other locations I now cover.
negativeExamples: Where do I find the MEC workweek deck?
I cannot submit my questionnaire.
Please remove this learner.

scenarios.description: A question about learning content or materials: Articulate 360 or Rise modules, PowerPoint or PDF resources, certification content, or capstone materials for FIT/FLO.
positiveExamples: The Rise module for week 4 will not open - is there a PDF version?
Where can I download the certification PPT for FIT?
The Articulate360 content is showing last year's material.
negativeExamples: Where is the MEC capstone deck on Schoox?
I cannot log in.
Please update my email address.

scenarios.description: The sender thanks the team or confirms that their issue has been resolved and they are able to work. No further action is needed.
positiveExamples: Thank you, that worked - I am able to work through the modules now.
All good now, confirmed access this morning.
This has been resolved, thanks for your help.
negativeExamples: Thank you in advance - could you please reset my access?
Thanks, but I still cannot submit the questionnaire.
Completed your request. Request ID: CR-1029.

scenarios.description: A learner's email address is incorrect, has changed, or a new address is now ready to be used in PEP Passport.
positiveExamples: My new email address is ready, please update it in PEP Passport.
The email address on this learner's record is incorrect.
I have had an email change - please update my profile.
negativeExamples: My manager's email is wrong on my profile.
Please remove this learner from FLO.
I cannot access my account.

scenarios.brdReference: Implementation decision AD-001 (satisfies FR-012, FR-032, BRD 10)
scenarios.description: The email does not match any of the twelve business scenarios with sufficient evidence, or the classifier returned UNKNOWN. Requires human intervention. This is not a BRD scenario - it exists so that nothing is forced into one of the twelve.
